_about: Light fighter (design doc, Initial unit roster: air). EVERY VALUE IS A PLACEHOLDER proposed by Track S on 2026-10-09 so the demo can fly; the unit design sheet and its variant boards replace them. Plausible for a WWII single-engine fighter (Spitfire, Bf 109, A6M class) at true scale. Record shape: data/units/_schema.json.
name: Light fighter

size_m._reason: Track S brief: a fighter about 9 m across (Bf 109 9.9 m span); the design doc's Scale section uses about 10 m for a fighter

draught_m._reason: a unit that does not float needs no water under it (the water rule, World.set_water, applies to domain sea only): 0

actions_per_turn._reason: Alex 2026-10-09 accepted this as the demo baseline. Was proposed: the most agile type gets the most decision points (design doc: faster units generally get more actions); 5 steps of 1 s in a 5 s turn

health._reason: light and fragile: the fewest pips of the three aircraft (Steambirds-style role trade-off)

sight_range_m._reason: Alex 2026-10-09 accepted the lead's fog recommendation (about 800 m so sight edges show at play zoom). Was proposed: about 15 s of flight at cruise ahead; unused until Track F's vision rule

material._reason: PROPOSED by builder G3 (2026-10-12; the board's table, variants/gunfire/board.json material_table, which Alex's decisions damage-looks, 'the model makes sense', and gunfire-looks, G3, put to use): an airframe is metal. Decides what a round that lands on it does (data/fx/fx.json gunfire): metal.

source_m._reason: one engine's smoke, not the wingspan (Alex, decision impact-by-round-and-target: puffs are not sized by the unit's length; the lead's 'about 8 m at most'). 8 m is close to the 9 m span the W1 puffs were drawn from, so a fighter's trail looks as it did

source_back_m._reason: where the smoke leaves the plane: 3 m behind its centre, the old 0.35 x 9 m (W1 tail_frac) kept

rise_mps._reason: ALEX (decision smoke-consistency, 2026-10-12), asked 'should planes' trails rise like ground smoke, and should the heavy fighter's and bomber's trails stay at their new, smaller size?': 'Yes to both'. So a plane's damage trail CLIMBS at 4 m/s, the same rate as a tank's, a boat's and the ruins' and wrecks' smolder (data/fx/fx.json ruin and crash smolder rise_mps), through the same model: a puff keeps the height it was born at, climbs and drifts with the wind at its height (fx_field.gd puff_drift), so an old puff of a low plane leans further downwind. It was 0 (PROPOSED by builder SMOKE, 2026-10-11: 'a puff climbing 4 m/s would lift an old puff by 100 m in its life'); Alex's answer ends that difference, and the fall trail of a plane out of control climbs with it (no jump at the moment it goes down). The number 4 is the ground smoke's, test_smoke_consistency holds the two equal

shape._about: One box. A plane's base is its BAND's absolute height (bands are absolute heights, data/sim/altitude.json), so the box reaches below and above it. Every number PROPOSED.

stamp._reason: a target, not scenery: other lines are not blocked by it

length_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 8 m, a single-engine fighter's fuselage (Bf 109 8.9 m)

width_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 9 m, the unit's size_m (the wingspan)

bottom_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 0.9 m under the band's height: the belly and wheels

top_m._reason: PROPOSED by builder LOF1 (2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire): 1.2 m over it: the canopy and fin

speed_min_mps._reason: stall about 160 km/h, typical of WWII single-engine fighters (140-170 km/h)

speed_max_mps._reason: 575 km/h level, a Spitfire or Bf 109 at low altitude

dive_speed_max_mps._reason: about 685 km/h; WWII fighters dived well past level top speed

accel_mps2._reason: cruise to top speed in 15 s (3 turns), stall to top in about 29 s (6 turns): 'several turns to reach top speed'

decel_mps2._reason: slows a little faster than it accelerates (drag helps, no airbrakes): 5 m/s per 1 s step

turn_rate_curve_dps._reason: about 20 deg/s at cruise (an 18 s circle, WWII sustained-turn territory), tighter when slow as Alex asked, 12 deg/s at top speed

turn_bleed_mps2._reason: more than its 4 m/s^2 of thrust: a full-rate turn at full power still loses 3 m/s every second, so a hard 180 at top speed ends near cruise

turn_bleed_exponent._reason: induced drag grows with the square of the load factor: a half-rate turn costs a quarter

bands_per_step._reason: one band per step keeps a climb a deliberate, visible choice

climb_speed_cost_mps._reason: a climb trades speed for height: a quarter of cruise per band

dive_speed_gain_mps._reason: less than the climb costs, so a climb-and-dive loses energy overall

round._reason: ALEX (decision weapon-kinds, 2026-10-11): 'Machine guns would be bullets which don't [explode].' A machine gun fires the bullet (data/sim/rounds.json), which draws a tracer (decision tracers-mg) and no G3 impact

hardpoints._reason: the lead's engagement-cones proposal (variants/engagement-cones/weapons_proposed.json), shown to Alex 2026-10-09, not yet decided. A fixed machine-gun PAIR, one hardpoint per wing, each rolling for itself

mount_deg._reason: the lead's engagement-cones proposal (variants/engagement-cones/weapons_proposed.json), shown to Alex 2026-10-09, not yet decided

half_across_deg._reason: the lead's engagement-cones proposal (variants/engagement-cones/weapons_proposed.json), shown to Alex 2026-10-09, not yet decided

elevation_deg._reason: the lead's engagement-cones proposal (variants/engagement-cones/weapons_proposed.json), shown to Alex 2026-10-09, not yet decided

half_height_deg._reason: the lead's engagement-cones proposal (variants/engagement-cones/weapons_proposed.json), shown to Alex 2026-10-09, not yet decided

effective_range_m._reason: the lead's engagement-cones proposal (variants/engagement-cones/weapons_proposed.json), shown to Alex 2026-10-09, not yet decided; Alex 2026-10-09: it is the EFFECTIVE range, inside which the range factor is 1, and a gun fires slightly over it at falling odds (data/sim/combat.json range_overshoot)

base_hit_chance._reason: Track C proposal (not in the lead's sheet): with two hardpoints at 2 rolls a second the pair makes about 0.56 hits a second on a centred target (2.8 pips a turn), so a light fighter takes about 3 turns of full chase to bring down the bomber's 8 pips

rim_odds_factor._reason: Track C proposal: a fixed gun is peaked (the lead's sheet: 'better near the centre'; Alex: a machine gun has better odds the closer the target is to the centre of its cone): a target on the rim has a fifth of the centre's odds

falloff_exponent._reason: Track C proposal: a quadratic fall (r squared) keeps the odds high through the inner half and drops them near the rim

tracking_dps._reason: Track C proposal (Alex 2026-10-10: relative velocity affects accuracy): the line-of-sight turn rate, degrees a second, at which crossing halves this gun's odds. A fixed gun is aimed by swinging the whole plane, so it tolerates little: 8 deg/s is a target crossing at 42 m/s from 300 m, about a 24 degree turn in a second; a target crossing at 100 m/s from 300 m (19 deg/s) leaves about 15 percent of the odds

damage_pips._reason: the lead's engagement-cones proposal (variants/engagement-cones/weapons_proposed.json), shown to Alex 2026-10-09, not yet decided

rolls_per_second._reason: Track C proposal (not in the lead's sheet): a machine-gun burst is a roll every half second (every second tick); two hardpoints, 20 rolls over a turn in the cone

drops._reason: Track S2 (2026-10-10): a fighter carries no bombs; the strike's bomb drop is a bomber's special

per_drop._reason: a fighter drops nothing: 0 bombs a drop, to match 0 drops
